answer: For a poll on the ripple effects of gale damage to saffron farms, officials check signatures against a frozen two-district voter roll. They accept one ballot per entry and reject invalid or repeated ballots. Each option scores the smaller of its two district counts. If it has 100 votes in one district and none in the other, reaching a score of 10 requires 10 votes in the latter, potentially costing recruitment effort. Shared keys and coordinated districts can still distort results.
